text:
Jordan: Need urgent help - my divorce decree says I must continue covering my ex-spouse on my employer health plan for 12 months as part of the settlement. Im mid open enrollment. How do I make sure they stay on and what docs do you need?
Priya (People Ops): Hi Jordan  thanks for the heads up. Thats a court-ordered continuation (not COBRA). Well need a copy of the divorce decree specifying the coverage requirement, plus any court order dates. Upload to the portal and tag People Ops.
Jordan: OK uploading the decree now. Do I enroll them through the regular dependent UI or is this handled differently?
Sam (Benefits): Good Q. Usually we process these as a special dependent exception. Well add them as a dependent on your plan with an administrative flag "court-ordered continuation" and note the required duration. Please also include the exs full legal name, DOB, and any other insurance information they may have.
Jordan: Will premiums still come out of my paycheck? The decree mentions the other partys responsibility for premiums but I want clarity so I don't get dinged.
Raj (Payroll): Payroll handles premiums per company policy and court instructions. If the decree requires the other party to reimburse you, we can assist with documentation but we don't bill third parties. Typically premiums continue to be deducted from your pay; any reimbursements would be between you and the other party. If the decree requires the employer to bill the ex directly, send that language and we'll route to Legal.
Legal (People Ops): If the decree mandates employer action (rare), upload the exact clause. Otherwise most decrees require the employee to maintain coverage and pursue reimbursement separately. We can confirm whether the decree imposes an obligation on the employer.
Jordan: What about effective date? It says "beginning on 2025-06-15 for 12 months"  can we retro to that date if I missed enrolling earlier?
Sam (Benefits): We can set the effective date to the court-ordered start if docs are provided within 30 days of the event or if the carrier permits retro effective for special cases. Upload the decree and well start a vendor exception. If the carrier allows retro coverage, claims will be coordinated accordingly.
BenefitsBot: KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/benefits/court-orders-continuation - lists docs carriers typically require (decree PDF, photo ID, SSN or ITIN, proof of residence) and notes about retro processing.
Jordan: The ex has an SSN but lives in a different state now. Will that be an issue?
Sam (Benefits): Not usually. We need their SSN or ITIN for enrollment and payroll records. Out-of-state residence is fine for coverage continuation; it may affect network access or out-of-network costs but benefits remain. If the ex has their own coverage, that will affect primary/secondary coordination. Upload their carrier card if they have one.
Priya (People Ops): Once you upload, well create an internal case and notify Benefits and Payroll. Expect a confirmation email within 3 business days. If the court requires employer notifications to the ex, let us know and well coordinate the standard carrier notices.
Jordan: Last one  if the decree requires the ex to reimburse me monthly, how should I track/payback?
Raj (Payroll): We dont handle third-party reimbursements. Many employees set up direct transfers or have the ex reimburse via bank transfer. If you need proof of premiums paid, Benefits can provide premium statements or a paystub history to support reimbursement.
Sam (Benefits): Case created #BP-CO-2211. Well review the decree and update coverage accordingly. Bring any follow-up docs (ID, SSN, proof of other coverage) into the portal thread and well process.
Jordan: Uploaded decree and exs ID. Thanks for the speedy responses :relieved:
Priya (People Ops): Youre all set for now. Well follow up if the carrier requires additional proof.
Jordan: Appreciate it everyone!
